title: Labor announces policy backflip to allow more backpackers to work in regional Australia
summary:
Number of people allowed to stay for third year on holiday maker visa to be increased from 5,000 to 25,000 under revised plan

  • Get our

blocks.text: The federal government is backpedaling on its plan to cut backpacker numbers following criticism from regional stakeholder groups who rely on the travellers for labour.
The Albanese government is expected on Tuesday to lift the proposed cap on third-year working holiday visas, boost regional work requirements and delay the start of a new ballot system.
The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, previously announced in September plans to cap the number of third year backpackers to 5,000 from the current level of about 31,000.
Industry sources said they expected the government to back down and instead set a cap at 25,000 places.
Burke was due to hold a press conference in Cairns on Tuesday morning.

The home affairs minister announced major reforms to working holiday visas in September including creating a ballot for backpackers seeking to stay a second or third year which would require them to work in the regions.

Under that proposal, just 45,000 backpackers would be allowed to remain for a second year and would be required to work at least three months in a regional area, and just 5,000 places would be allocated for workers seeking to remain in Australia for a third year.
Industry sources expected second year backpackers will be required to work in regional areas for four months, instead of three, and that the ballot will be delayed.
The changes follow months of consultation with industry, regional and agricultural groups who warned of worker shortages under the crackdown.

Workers from the UK are exempt from the caps under the free trade agreement signed in 2021. Sources says the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, is in discussions with his UK counterpart, Andy Burnham, to force British backpackers to also do regional work going forward.
One industry source said they welcomed the anticipated announcement which showed the government was “listening to the concerns from our sector”.
